findings.text: MUST-FIX. A configured root can still be dropped or retargeted silently, because REQUIRED_MODULE_ROOTS (lines 18-24) is a verbatim copy of MODULE_ROOTS (lines 12-16) three lines below it in the same file. The anchor refuses a ONE-SIDED edit and I proved that rather than inferring it: deleting imas_codex/standard_names/export.py from MODULE_ROOTS only fails with 'AssertionError: required module roots are missing: frozenset({PosixPath('imas_codex/standard_names/export.py')})', 1 failed 2 passed (mutation-c-root-dropped-one-red.log). It does not refuse a TWO-SIDED edit. CONCRETE TRIGGERING INPUT A: delete the export.py line from BOTH tuples - measured 3 passed (mutation-d-root-dropped-both.log; remaining aperture 10 modules >= MINIMUM_SCANNED_MODULES 8, 27 candidates >= MINIMUM_LITERAL_DEFAULTED_GETATTRS 24, each surviving root candidate_count > 0). CONCRETE TRIGGERING INPUT B, the sharp one: replace Path('imas_codex/standard_names/review') with Path('imas_codex/standard_names/fanout') in BOTH tuples - measured 3 passed (mutation-e-root-retargeted-clean-both.log). fanout is 9 modules and 16 candidates with zero violations, so module_count is 11 and candidate_count 28, every per-root assertion holds, and the ENTIRE review package - the surface that motivated this node and the one that held the original pipeline.py defect - leaves the scan with the suite green. I checked that this substitution is not a contrivance: a census of every imas_codex subtree (clean-roots-census.log) lists 8 roots with candidates and no violations, so a green substitute is easy to reach by accident as well as on purpose. A retarget to imas_codex/discovery does fail, but only by accident - the production test finds 10 real violations there, while test_configured_module_roots_have_coverage itself PASSES under that mutation (mutation-b-root-retargeted-both.log), which is the direct demonstration that the anchor does not detect retargeting. REMEDY: derive the required set from something with an independent reason to exist rather than from a second copy of the literal - for example assert that the scanned module list contains imas_codex/standard_names/review/pipeline.py by name, so the anchor names a file the guard exists to cover rather than restating the tuple.

MUST-FIX, evidence accuracy. The archived section 'The guard proves it inspected a non-empty aperture' still records that 'the static guard now asserts floors of at least 8 scanned modules, 3,000 declared class attributes and 24 literal three-argument candidates' and that the receipt shows '4,013 declared attributes'. Commit 486dfc17f DELETED MINIMUM_DECLARED_CLASS_ATTRIBUTES and removed declared_attribute_count from DefaultedAttributeScan, and the correction commit e1ab3df81 added a new section without retiring this one. CONCRETE TRIGGERING INPUT: a reader follows the figure to the code - git grep -n 'MINIMUM_DECLARED_CLASS_ATTRIBUTES|declared_attribute_count' HEAD -- tests/ imas_codex/ returns nothing, and git show HEAD:docs/evidence/archive/sn-lifecycle-integrity-landed.html | grep -c '3,000 declared class attributes' returns 1. The archive asserts a guard that does not exist. Note the DELETION itself is correct and is the best part of this correction: that floor was on the mask rather than on the aperture, and it was load-bearing on four gitignored generated files - measured here, a git-archive tree without them yields 2,767 declared attributes (clean-roots-census.log) against 4,014 in the checkout, so the deleted floor would have failed on any tree lacking the generated models. The defect is that the record was not corrected with the code.

Moderate, and the answer to the wave's 'does the new invariant hold at EVERY construction site including fallback paths' question. The fallback path CHANGED DIRECTION in this correction and the change is not noted anywhere. Before 486dfc17f, _python_modules appended a non-existent configured path unconditionally ('else: modules.append(candidate)'), so a misspelled root raised FileNotFoundError from module.read_text() - loud. After it, _python_modules returns [] for a path that is neither dir nor file (line 64), so a misspelled root contributes silently nothing. Refusal is now delegated entirely to the sibling test: only test_configured_module_roots_have_coverage reads scan.roots and asserts root.exists. test_defaulted_literal_attributes_are_declared reads scan.violations alone. CONCRETE TRIGGERING INPUT, read from the source at HEAD rather than measured: misspell all three entries in both tuples (loop.py -> loop_.py and so on) and run only 'pytest tests/standard_names/test_defaulted_attributes_exist.py::test_defaulted_literal_attributes_are_declared' - every root yields [] modules, violations is [] and the guard is green while scanning nothing. The coverage test catches it in a whole-file run, so this is a selection-dependent rather than an unconditional hole; making _defaulted_attribute_scan itself raise on a configured root that does not resolve would put the invariant at the construction site instead of in one of two callers.

SOUND, and it is the correction that matters. The fixture test closes the predicate-inversion hole the prior review scored MUST-FIX, and I verified it by making the guarded thing happen rather than by reading a green suite. In a git-archive scratch copy at HEAD the file is 3 passed (scratch-control-green.log, the positive control that the instrument sees something known present). Applying the prior review's exact triggering input - replacing 'attribute_name not in declared_attributes' at line 149 with 'False' - now gives '1 failed, 2 passed', failing test_defaulted_literal_attribute_fixture_is_reported (mutation-a-predicate-inverted-red.log). The fixture is independent of production code: it writes imas_codex/standard_names/review/fixture.py under tmp_path, so _declared_class_attributes walks an imas_codex tree containing no classes and the expected finding cannot be masked by a repository-wide declaration. Line 215's 'scan.candidate_count == 1' additionally pins the aperture, so a mutation that stops collecting candidates is refused by the same test. This is a permanent counterexample, not a one-off control, and it is what makes the disabled guard and the working guard distinguishable from here on.

Minor, unfixed from the prior review. The two surviving aggregate floors at lines 183-184 still carry no assertion message, while every assertion the correction ADDED in the same function (lines 178, 179, 186, 187, 190) carries one. CONCRETE TRIGGERING INPUT: a future refactor that moves candidate getattr calls out of loop.py drops candidate_count below 24 and the failure prints 'assert 23 >= 24' with nothing saying whether the source tree shrank legitimately or the scan went blind - exactly the ambiguity the added messages elsewhere were written to remove. The fence asked for per-root coverage 'replacing' aggregate floors; the node kept both, which is the right call because per-root '> 0' does not imply the totals, but the two retained floors should be brought up to the same reporting standard as their neighbours.

SOUND, answering the fence's third question directly: the recorded sensitivity limitation DOES state a figure a reader can check rather than a general caution. 'What a green result still cannot say' names the population (the five defaulted reads in _extract_audit_findings), the catch count (findings and affected_names), and the three specific misses by name (severity, message, category), together with the mechanism - resolution against the union of fields and properties on every class in imas_codex rather than against the receiver type. A reader can re-derive 2 of 5 from those names. Two caveats worth recording rather than fixing: the figure is now historical, because the five reads were repaired at integrated main and git show HEAD:imas_codex/standard_names/review/pipeline.py returns no getattr line carrying any of the five names, so the check must be run against base 9a5e40f4b; and the limitation is stated as a count over one motivating function rather than as a rate over the 30 candidates the configured aperture actually scans, so it bounds the known case without bounding the guard.

Wave question - does any existing test assert the behaviour the corrections replaced? No, and I checked rather than assumed. The corrections deleted MINIMUM_DECLARED_CLASS_ATTRIBUTES and DefaultedAttributeScan.declared_attribute_count and changed _python_modules from taking a tuple of roots to taking one root; git grep at HEAD returns zero hits for either deleted name anywhere under tests/ or imas_codex/, and _python_modules and _defaulted_attribute_scan have no caller outside this file (_undeclared_defaulted_attributes at line 169 uses the default argument, the fixture test at line 213 passes an explicit tuple). Nothing asserts the old floor and nothing should - the old floor was the defect. Scope is clean: the three correction commits touch tests/standard_names/test_defaulted_attributes_exist.py and two HTML records only, with no production source in the diff.

justifications.durability: Substantially improved over the 11 this node previously scored, and not closed. Measured, not inferred: predicate inversion is now REFUSED (1 failed) where it was previously silent; a one-sided root drop is REFUSED with the exact intended message; a two-sided root drop is ACCEPTED (3 passed); a two-sided retarget from the review package to standard_names/fanout is ACCEPTED (3 passed) and takes the guard's primary surface out of scope with every floor and every per-root assertion still satisfied. A census shows 8 candidate-bearing violation-free subtrees available as green substitutes, so the escape is reachable without intent. Separately, the fallback path in _python_modules changed from raising on a missing root to returning [], so scanning nothing is silent inside the scan function itself and is caught only by the sibling coverage test.
justifications.evidence: The node's own receipts are specific and reproducible, and I reproduced the decisive one independently: the prior review's exact inversion input now fails. Two negative controls with named mutations, a focused restored gate, and a full tests/standard_names/ comparison of FAILED/ERROR identifier lines are recorded. The deduction is that the archive's aperture section now describes deleted constants and a deleted scan field, so part of the landed record is false against the code it describes - and that section is the one a reader would check first, because it is where the figures are.
justifications.fit: Idiomatic for this suite: a frozen ModuleRootScan per root, a default argument that keeps the production caller unchanged while letting the fixture pass an arbitrary root, and assertion messages on every new assertion. Two blemishes. REQUIRED_MODULE_ROOTS duplicates MODULE_ROOTS as a literal rather than deriving from anything, which is what makes the two-sided edit invisible. The two retained aggregate floors are the only messageless assertions left in the function, which the prior review already raised.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The two corrections the fence named were both delivered and both do what was asked. The synthetic fixture (line 207) gives the violation predicate a permanent input that makes it fire, which is the exact gap the prior review scored MUST-FIX, and the per-root coverage assertions (lines 185-192) replace membership-blind aggregates with a per-root exists / module_count > 0 / candidate_count > 0 contract. The deletion of MINIMUM_DECLARED_CLASS_ATTRIBUTES is an unrequested improvement that retires a floor pointed the wrong way. The verdict is MUST-FIX only because the root anchor delivered alongside them is a copy of the tuple it anchors, so the durability question the corrections exist to answer is closed in one direction and open in the other.
justifications.scope_discipline: Exemplary. The three correction commits touch only the assigned test file and the two HTML records; no production source appears in any diff, and the previously identified pipeline.py reads were left to the repair that landed independently at integrated main rather than folded in. Follow-ons - the type-unaware name union and the two pipeline.py attributes - are recorded with file, line and status. The one scope-adjacent miss is a record not updated to match the node's own later commit, which is inside scope rather than outside it.
